title: Home Mortgage Loans: Scope and Duration of Mortgage Insurance
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Scope and Duration of Mortgage Insurance

Mortgage insurance on Home Mortgage Loans takes different forms by program: private mortgage insurance (PMI) in the programs that provide for it, the FHA annual mortgage insurance premium (MIP), and nothing monthly at all on VA loans. This page describes when each applies, how long it lasts without any action by the borrower, and what changes in the payment once it stops.

## Clauses

**Where PMI applies.** PMI is carried only in a program that sets a PMI loan-to-value threshold, and only on a loan whose loan-to-value at origination was above that threshold.

**Automatic end of PMI.** No request is needed for PMI to end on schedule. It terminates on the date on which the scheduled balance reaches the program's automatic termination percentage of the original property value, if the loan is current on that date. If the loan is not current on that date, PMI terminates on the first day of the month following the date the loan becomes current.

**FHA MIP.** The FHA annual premium stops after the program's stated number of years only for a loan whose original loan-to-value was 90 percent or less. For any higher original loan-to-value, the premium lasts for the whole life of the loan.

**VA loans.** A VA loan has no monthly mortgage insurance.

**Effect on the payment.** The monthly mortgage insurance premium is collected within the escrow payment. When insurance comes off — by a granted cancellation, by automatic termination, or by the end of FHA MIP — the monthly premium drops to zero and the escrow payment falls by that premium, starting with the next installment.

## Branching questions

**An FHA loan began at 88 percent loan-to-value (hypothetical). Does its MIP ever end?** Yes. 88 is 90 or less, so the premium ends once the program's stated years have run.

**An FHA loan began at 93 percent loan-to-value (hypothetical). Does its MIP ever end?** No. The original loan-to-value was above 90 percent, so the premium runs for the life of the loan.

**Does automatic termination depend on today's market value?** No. It is tied to the scheduled balance measured against the original property value.

## Timing illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- The schedule shows the balance reaching the automatic termination percentage on 1 October, and the loan is current that day. PMI terminates on 1 October.
- The same balance point is reached on 1 October while the loan is past due; the loan becomes current on 12 November. PMI terminates on 1 December, the first day of the month after the loan became current.

The loan-to-value figures and dates here are invented for illustration.
